title: [3.13] gh-157335: Fix out-of-bounds write in mmap.mmap.__setitem__ (#157438)
live_proof: measured, not asserted: the trigger runs on the pinned 3.13.7 ASan build (PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0) and reports ASAN:SEGV in safe_byte_copy (mmapmodule.c:361). Running it is the liveness proof -- a sanitizer report here means the defect is present in this tree.
fidelity: the trigger is upstream's own reproducer from the issue, run through the real interpreter rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it.
allocator_layer: mmap mapping (mmapmodule.c); no allocator issues this object, so no pymalloc pool is involved in any configuration
layer_note: The ASan nesting test is structurally inconclusive here and that is expected: the buffer IS the mmap mapping, so a write past its end reaches the guard page and ASan reports SEGV rather than a heap region, with PYTHONMALLOC unset and with PYTHONMALLOC=malloc alike. allocator_consumed is 'no' on the mapping's provenance, not on that test.

virtual-malloc.oracle: virtual profile, pymalloc stock on musl mallocng (tools/arms.json virtual-cpython): a fault in one of the case's fault_sites, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it

virtual-nested-pools.oracle: virtual profile, pymalloc on its lifetime port, CPY_SUBLET_MODE=1 (tools/arms.json virtual-cpython-pools): as virtual-malloc

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: a bounds fault, SIGPROT si_code=1 (PROT_CHERI_BOUNDS), at the write past the end of the mapping, if the mapping's capability is bounded to the requested length. No allocator issues this object, so revocation has nothing to act on.

status: measured on three arms; matrix rows in results/20261006/matrix.tsv: spatial NOTIMPL [delivered=no] (spatial-20261006-105111); sublet NOTIMPL [delivered=no] (sublet-20261006-123446); cheribsd-revocation SILENT [delivered=held-out] (cheri11)

That run uses no Capstone arm and was recorded before any virtual arm ran.
